chapter_title: Open File Formats and Version Control
learning_objective: The learner will practice writing Markdown for four structures (a heading, a list, a link, and an image with alt text), with at least 3 of 4 tasks passing on the first Check.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** markdown-practice-lab
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** practice
**Learning Objective:** The learner will practice writing Markdown for four structures (a heading, a list, a link, and an image with alt text), with at least 3 of 4 tasks passing on the first Check. **Prerequisites:** Markdown, Source Format, Open File Format (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each task the learner edits the text and presses Check. A task passes when the live preview contains the required structure exactly as described in the Requirement column of Content. Mastery is at least 3 of 4 tasks passing on the first Check. Using the hint is allowed and is shown in the score. **Misconceptions:** (1) Markdown needs special software to write. (2) The square brackets in an image hold the file name. (3) Alt text is optional because the image is already on the page. **Instructional Rationale:** Practice with immediate feedback is the right pattern for an Apply-level skill. A live preview shows each symbol's effect as the learner types, so the learner links the symbol to the structure instead of memorizing a list. **Content:** The four tasks, in this order: | # | Task | Starting text | Requirement | Hint (shown on request) | Message when it fails | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Make a heading | Water Cycle | The preview contains a level-2 heading whose text is exactly "Water Cycle". | Start the line with two pound signs and a space. | "The heading needs two pound signs, a space, and the text Water Cycle." | | 2 | Make a list | evaporation, condensation, and precipitation, one per line | The preview contains a bulleted list of exactly three items, in the order evaporation, condensation, precipitation. | Start each line with a hyphen and a space. | "Each item needs a hyphen and a space at the start of its own line." | | 3 | Add a link | The words Watershed Basics and the address https://example.org/watershed-basics | The preview contains a link whose visible text is exactly "Watershed Basics" and whose address is https://example.org/watershed-basics. | Put the visible text in square brackets and the address in parentheses right after it. | "The link needs square brackets around the words and parentheses around the address." | | 4 | Add an image with alt text | The address https://example.org/images/river.png and the words A river flowing through a valley | The preview contains an image whose address is https://example.org/images/river.png and whose alt text is exactly "A river flowing through a valley". | Write an exclamation mark, then square brackets holding the alt text, then the address in parentheses. | "The image needs an exclamation mark first, then the alt text in brackets, then the address in parentheses." | The Markdown symbols the lab teaches: two pound signs and a space for a level-2 heading, a hyphen and a space for a bullet, square brackets then parentheses for a link, and an exclamation mark before that pattern for an image. **Provenance:** The tasks are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels the addresses "example addresses". The symbols follow the chapter section "Markdown". **Rules:** A task passes only when the preview shows the required structure with the exact text or address. Extra text elsewhere in the editor does not fail a task. The learner may press Check as many times as they like. Only a pass on the first Check counts toward mastery, and later passes are shown as passed with hint or retry. **Learner Activity:** 1. The sim shows task 1, with the starting text in the editor and the live preview beside it. 2. The learner edits the text and watches the preview change. 3. The learner presses Check. The sim shows pass or fail with the message. 4. The learner may open the hint at any time. 5. After a pass the sim shows task 2, and so on through task 4. **Feedback:** 4 tasks in the fixed order. Pass: "Task passed: the preview shows [requirement]". Fail: the message in the table for that task. The summary shows "[n] of 4 tasks passed on the first Check, and [m] needed a retry or a hint". At 3 or more first-Check passes it adds "You can write the four Markdown structures." Below 3 it lists the tasks that needed a retry. **Starting State:** Task 1 with the text Water Cycle in the editor and an empty-structure preview. The question shown is "Make this line a level-2 heading." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's Markdown example uses the heading "Water Cycle", a list of evaporation, condensation, and precipitation, the link text "Watershed Basics" with the address https://example.org/watershed-basics, and an image with the alt text "A river flowing through a valley".
